question: Let $A$ be the set of all numbers which can be represented as the sum of three consecutive positive integers. What is the greatest common divisor of all numbers in $A$?
solution:
For a positive integer \(k\), the sum of the three consecutive integers starting at \(k\) is \(k+(k+1)+(k+2)=3(k+1)\). Thus 3 divides every member of \(A\). Taking \(k=1\) and \(k=2\) gives 6 and 9, so any common divisor must also divide \(9-6=3\). Hence the greatest common divisor is 3.
Final answer: 3
